cover.headline_html: 3 myths that kill new GovCon shops.

myths.label: The Past-Performance Trap
myths.myth_text: You can't win federal contracts without prior federal performance.
myths.reality_text: Teaming agreements let new shops partner with established primes — you inherit their track record. Mentor-protégé programs work the same way. The first contract is rarely won alone.

myths.label: The Set-It-Forget-It Myth
myths.myth_text: Getting on the GSA Schedule means contracts will come to you.
myths.reality_text: The Schedule is a pre-approved vendor list, not a lead machine. It removes the barrier to entry — but selling, follow-up, and BD are still yours to own.

myths.label: The Time-and-Cost Lie
myths.myth_text: The GSA Schedule costs too much and takes too long to be worth it.
myths.reality_text: Most small businesses spend $5K–$15K and 6–9 months to get approved. Once on, the Schedule is valid for 20 years. The question isn't what it costs to get in — it's what you lose by staying out.

close.close_question: Drop the biggest GovCon myth you believed before you started pursuing federal contracts.
